rationale: Independently upheld as the exact qualified working-text whole-case claim, not because either blind arm detected a planted error. The complete EO 7420 text identifies William T. Marshall, office-man in the Federal Emergency Administration of Public Works, closing number 7420 and signing date July 20, 1936. Its recital and operative sentence both limit the exemption and continuance to August 1, 1937. The exact ending span 1325:1386 agrees with first_end.date and whole_order_end.date 1937-08-01 in this genuine claim. The inventory is complete: one combined personal exemption/continuance; the statutory quotation supplies authority, and the public-interest and retirement-age recitals add no independent presidential command or concrete earlier-ending condition. The calendar limit applies to the combined grant, rather than merely to performance of an act. It operates without proof of actual continued service. Earlier death, resignation, retirement, separation, repeal or revocation is not established; no uninterrupted employment is inferred. Public interest is stated as the basis of the grant, not as an express ongoing condition with an unresolved earlier cessation. The full EO 7629 text, signed June 8, 1937, expressly identifies the same person, position and EO 7420 of July 20, 1936, and makes its own further exemption/continuance until August 1, 1938. It neither expressly revokes nor substitutes a date in EO 7420; its signing and ending dates do not displace the original grant's own calendar ending. No independent continuing rule, office, post-term duty or savings clause preserves operative authority. Possible compensation or credit from service actually performed is an accrued consequence, not proof of service or a surviving command. The terminated clause state and no-current-operative-force conclusion at October 14, 2026 follow from that fixed whole-command limit on the bounded record. No affirmative current authority is asserted, so no continuing enabling-law predicate is used to establish present force. Search declarations supply qualified counterevidence coverage, not exhaustive absence proof. The calendar date is supported; the disclosed inclusive/exclusive intraday alternatives are not independently resolved. Original authentication, replacement/requotation and human-review limitations remain.
